IEF미국 중기국채 (7-10년)매도종가 92.25
추천: 매도 기계적 규칙에 따라 종가(92.25)가 트레일링 스탑(92.54) 아래로 명백히 이탈했으므로 청산(매도)한다. 20일·100일 상단 돌파도 모두 거짓이어서 신규 진입 조건은 성립하지 않는다. 일목균형표가 구름 아래·음운으로 보조 지표 역시 하락 추세를 뒷받침하므로 리스크 관리상 비중 축소 여지 없이 전량 청산이 원칙이다. 뉴스 흐름도 이 청산 신호와 배치되지 않는다. 블룸버그 기사(“US Treasuries Fall After Payrolls Beat…”)는 8월 고용 지표 호조로 연준 금리 인상 베팅이 강화되면서 2년물 금리가 8bp 급등(가격 하락)했다고 전한다 — 단기 금리 민감도가 큰 IEF 가격 하락의 직접적 촉매다. 로이터/힌두비즈니스라인 기사(“Why US Treasury yields may stay high…”)는 구조적 공급 과잉(연방 부채 40조 달러 근접)과 가격 민감형 매수자 비중 확대로 텀 프리미엄이 상승해 장기 금리 하락이 제한적임을 지적한다 — 펀더멘털상으로도 채권 가격 반등 모멘텀이 약함을 확인시켜 준다. 월러 총재 발언으로 금리가 소폭 하락했다는 기사도 있으나, 이는 일시적 되돌림에 그쳤고 이후 고용 지표와 구조적 수급 악화로 다시 상승 압력이 우세해졌음을 앞서 두 기사가 보여준다. 따라서 뉴스는 기계적 청산 신호를 지지하는 팩트로 읽히며, 노이즈로 치부할 성격이 아니다.

Why lower Treasury yields could require a weaker economy: analysis
Matt Peterson · 2026-09-04T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: The piece argues that U.S. long-term Treasury yields remain high even as the White House seeks to lower them. Key drivers are: ongoing deficits and concerns about Fed independence, and investors demanding more compensation to hold Treasuries. AI infrastructure spending and tech corporate debt add to capital competition. Lower yields may only come with a weaker economy, which would reduce borrowing costs but hinder growth. The 10-year yield has hovered near 4.8%, with the Treasury increasing long-term buybacks to improve liquidity. Real (inflation-adjusted) yields have risen, signaling that stronger real growth rather than monetary policy alone may be lifting yields. A potential economic slowdown could cool borrowing costs, but that outcome would be unfavorable for growth. The deficit outlook remains large (CBO projects about $2.1 trillion this year), supporting ongoing elevated borrowing. Overall, the yields imply a delicate balance: higher compensation for risk and structural deficits keep yields elevated, while any easing would likely require weaker economic activity.

Why US Treasury yields may stay high despite efforts to lower borrowing costs - The HinduBusinessLine
Reuters · 2026-09-02T00:00:00.000Z

Here’s a concise, user-focused summary of the article on US Treasury yields: - Long-term US Treasury yields are likely to stay elevated despite efforts to lower borrowing costs. - Key drivers: persistent inflation concerns, growing bond supply from governments and high-quality issuers, and a shift in demand toward buyers who require higher yields. - Structural market changes: the mix of buyers is shifting away from price-insensitive, long-horizon holders (e.g., certain overseas lenders or official sectors) toward more price-sensitive participants, increasing term premiums and volatility. - The “term premium”—the extra yield investors demand to lock in decades-long exposure—has risen, aiding higher yields. - Deteriorating US fiscal outlook (federal debt approaching $40 trillion) further supports higher term premiums. - Treasury attempts to lower long-term costs may be limited by these structural supply/demand dynamics, which are partly outside policymakers’ control. - Markets also factor in inflation uncertainty and external risks (e.g., energy price pressures from geopolitical events) that complicate yield containment. - Overall view: unless structural demand/supply dynamics shift materially, a meaningful, sustained drop in long-term yields is unlikely in the near term. If you want, I can pull a focused verdict on the near-term odds for a specific horizon (e.g., next 3–6 months) or compare this view with other analyses.

US Treasuries Fall After Payrolls Beat, Traders Raise Fed Rate Bets - Bloomberg
Michael MacKenzie · 2026-09-04T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: - US Treasuries fell after stronger-than-expected August payrolls, fueling bets that the Federal Reserve will raise rates later this month. - Yields rose across maturities, led by the two-year note up about eight basis points to 4.416% and the five-year around 5.58%. Moves reversed somewhat later in the session. - The move reflects traders pricing in higher Federal Reserve rate expectations, with near-term maturities more sensitive to policy changes than longer ones. If you’re looking for a bonds-only outlook: - Short-duration yields (2-year) show the strongest sensitivity to Fed rate hikes; a continued jobs strength scenario could push policy expectations higher and keep the curve bid up in the short end. - Intermediate-term yields (5-year) also moved higher, signaling a shifting repricing across the curve. - Longer-dated Treasuries may follow if the market maintains hawkish Fed expectations, though longer maturities often respond more to growth and inflation surprises than immediate rate moves.

The Kolb Investment Group - RBC Wealth Management - Dog days of policymaking
us.rbcwealthmanagement.com · 2026-09-04T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: The piece critiques a proposed U.S. Treasury bond-buyback program led by Scott Bessent, arguing it is unlikely to meaningfully lower long-term yields. Key points: - The plan to double buybacks to $4 billion per operation lacks a concrete yield target and fails to specify funding and price clarity. - With tens of trillions in debt, the modest buybacks don’t meaningfully change the supply-demand dynamics; accounting gimmicks don’t alter intervention size. - Without a clear price line, market participants can misprice value, undermining effectiveness. - Bessent’s intervention would mostly slow the speed of a selloff rather than suppress yields; it risks signaling reduced credibility and could weaken the U.S. dollar. - Long-term yields currently reflect concerns about fiscal policy, inflation, and political stability. Sustainable lower yields would require credible fiscal restraint (reducing deficits) and policy stability, beyond a buyback program. - The piece warns that market credibility is essential for 30-year bonds; artificial interventions could undermine confidence if not paired with credible long-term policies.

Treasury yields fall after Fed's Waller signals support for no rate hike
Sean Conlon,Hugh Leask · 2026-09-03T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: - U.S. Treasury yields edged lower across the curve after Fed Governor Christopher Waller signaled support for holding rates steady at the upcoming policy meeting. - 10-year yield fell to about 4.77% (roughly -2 bps), 30-year yield around 5.25% (about -1 bp), and 2-year yield declined to ~4.34% (about -4 bps). - Waller acknowledged inflation remains above target but indicated disinflation signs and a potential backdrop for pausing rate hikes if data stay on trend. - The move comes after a prior run-up in yields due to concerns over debt, inflation, and higher energy prices; yields were near multi-year highs before the dip. - Overall outlook: near-term yields may remain sensitive to upcoming data on inflation and disinflation trends, with traders pricing in the possibility of a steady rate stance at the next Fed meeting.
